counterfactual_missing_items: No raw support for a broader coronary artery disease label
No raw support for left main coronary artery disease as a primary diagnosis
No raw support for right coronary artery occlusion as a primary diagnosis
decisive_items: Cardiac troponin I level was 25 ng/mL (normal, <0.023 ng/mL)
ST-segment elevation in leads III and aVR, Q wave in lead III, and ST-segment depression in leads I, II, aVL, aVF, and V2 to V6
total occlusion of the right coronary artery (RCA) and subtotal occlusion of the left main coronary artery (LMCA)
response.rationale: R2 is the only candidate with raw support directly indicating acute myocardial infarction via elevated troponin and characteristic ECG changes. R4 and R3 only cite isolated angiography findings, which are components of the MI diagnosis but not the diagnosis itself. R5 has no raw support and is a vague umbrella term. Thus R2 is the clear champion.

rejected.why: Only cites RCA occlusion, which is a finding, not a diagnosis; lacks raw evidence for the overall clinical picture.
Only cites LMCA subtotal occlusion, similarly a finding, not a diagnosis; insufficient for the most likely diagnosis.
No raw support spans; relies on generator assessments and is too broad, not specific to the case.
